text:
nora: Quick thought thread — proposing a "micro-crumb" pattern: compress org/workspace into a single compact element, show the first two visible trail items (Serving / Overview), and expose deeper anchors as shareable hash paths (e.g. /.../serving/overview#traffic). Goal: save horizontal real-estate without losing linkability.

ben: I'm into saving space. One question: hash anchors vs path segments — hashes are cheap but some internal routing libs treat them specially. How do we handle server-side previews and SEO?

otto: Tech note: our app is SPA; using hash anchors avoids server config changes, but path segments are cleaner for copy/paste. We could support both: canonicalize to path on share actions, accept either on load. Implement client-side normalization on initial navigation (replaceState).

irene: Accessibility: if we open a deep anchor, we must move focus to the anchored region and send a brief aria-live polite message like "Navigated to Traffic". Also truncated micro-crumbs need accessible labels and an explicit expand control (not hover-only).

nora: UX idea: micro-crumb when focused shows a small popup list with full org and workspace links; the control is keyboard tabbable and has aria-expanded. For mobile, it becomes a single row with a chevron to expand.

ben: Edge case: what about anonymous share links coming from external apps — if they hit /.../serving/overview#traffic and the user is not signed-in, we redirect to auth then restore the hash. Need to ensure our auth redirect preserves the anchor (some browsers drop hash on server redirect). We should prefer path-based canonicalization for that flow.

otto: Good catch. Browser behaviour: hash isn't sent to server, so we must stash the hash in the query before redirect, then rebuild the final path after auth. Slightly clunky but doable. We'll capture window.location.hash -> ?_anchor=traffic during redirect.

irene: For screen readers, prefer path navigation if possible because some ATs announce path changes better. But the move/focus and aria-live will cover the experience either way.

nora: Proposal for canonicalization rules (rough):
```
1) Accept both /.../serving/overview#panel and /.../serving/overview/panel on load.
2) On user-initiated share action, convert to canonical path /.../serving/overview/panel and copy that.
3) For incoming hash-based links that require auth, encode as ?_anchor=panel before redirect, then restore to canonical path after auth.
```

ben: Metrics to track: share-method (hash vs path), anchor-restore-success, auth-redirect-anchor-loss. Also track micro-crumb expand rate and keyboard usage.

deploy-bot: Canary preview deployed: https://canary.console.redwood.ai/microcrumbs (may require SSO).

irene: Motion notes: micro-crumb expand should be instant (no large layout shifts). Use transform/opacity for the popup; put it in a portal so we don't reflow the rail. Keyboard escape should collapse and return focus to the micro-crumb button.

otto: Dev checklist: router accepts alias patterns, normalizer middleware that maps hash->path on first load (replaceState), focus manager util to restore scroll position for lists, tests for auth flow anchor persistence.

nora: I'll draft the spec and small mockups and post them here. Plan: 2-week feature-flagged canary rollout, keep legacy /models and /deployments aliases for 90 days. Thanks all — tag me with any gotchas.
